# Dialects

> Dialects is an open-source OKLCH design-token system by Nerando Johnson (@Nerajno) for developingdvlpr.com: one layer of CSS custom properties shared by every site, with four surface dialects (portfolio, learn, teach, build) that change only a few "dial" variables (font, density and two accent colours), in light and dark mode.

Key facts:

- Package: `@nerajno/dialects`, installed from GitHub tags: `npm i github:Nerajno/dvlpr-dialects#v0.1.0`
- Files: `tokens.css` (the spine), `utilities.css`, `code.css` (Shiki css-variables theme), `fonts.css`, `theme-init.js` (sets surface and mode before first paint), `tailwind-preset.cjs` (Tailwind CSS 3.4+)
- Colour is written in `oklch()`; hex values are nearest-sRGB references for design tools.
- Each surface has an action accent (`--accent`, for links, buttons and focus) and a support accent (`--accent-2`, for tags, highlights and code strings).
- Accent names: portfolio Quiet Violet and Signal Indigo; learn Notebook Ochre and Highlighter Plum; teach Chalkboard Teal and Pink Chalk; build Workshop Orange and Blueprint Blue.
- Status colours: Go Green (ok), Caution Yellow (warn), Stop Red (error), Notice Blue (info), each paired with a marker shape.
- Contrast: text tokens and `--accent` reach at least 4.5:1 on every background; `--border-strong` at least 3:1.

## Docs

- [Style guide](https://nerajno.github.io/dvlpr-dialects/): every token, type style and component, live, on all four surfaces in light and dark
